_how: Recipe for shorts.build (video-machine). 12 clips from Brandon Enervold's (Bismarck-Septic-Excavating) guest episode, take 150507 (Zoom HD 1280x720, speaker view, no upscale). Source is the lip-synced file (zoom-150507-synced.mov, Brandon 43 ms earlier) with its words file; keep = inclusive word-index ranges in play order (splits drop Ashley's questions or a talking-through-it phrase); fillers skip automatically; stammers stay in the audio and are hidden from the captions with "" fixes rather than cut, and max_gap 1.0, so the clips stay smooth (Ashley's Oct 2026 notes). layout crop at 0.5 (Ashley sits at about 0.45 of the frame, Brandon 0.57). Posting plan: release week 2026-11-04..11-10, every clip to YouTube + TikTok at noon or 5 PM CT; the five strongest also to Instagram and Facebook at noon on weekdays. Captions: one per network; {bse} tags Bismarck-Septic-Excavating (its site links only a Facebook page, id 61568685107784; no Instagram, TikTok or YouTube found), the full episode linked ({episode}) everywhere but Facebook. approved = Ashley approved it in Ops. Clip edges were measured on each person's own Zoom track (Whisper ran words together across real pauses, so the build's cut landed inside a word): trim_start below 0 moves a start earlier to keep a first syllable the cut clipped, above 0 skips the tail of the word before; end_pad lets the last word finish. ten-feet-deep, freeze-ups and tank-collapsed play straight through (stammers hidden from the captions) instead of cutting mid-word, and market-sooner keeps Ashley's 'That's great advice' because Brandon's closing line starts 0.5 s after Whisper's time. Instagram Reel covers (Ashley's style A, 2026-10-28): 07_notes/shorts/covers/<id>.jpg, built by video-machine shorts.covers from the frames in shorts.json cover_at.

Most homes around Bismarck were built in the '90s, and he says once H2S has been rotting out a tank that sits 8 feet in the ground, digging it up for a repair is sometimes not the best idea. clips.title:
Why our septic tanks
sit *10 feet* down

youtube.title: Why some North Dakota septic tanks sit 10 feet underground
What septic work looks like at 40 below in North Dakota

captions.instagram:
How cold does it get? 40 below, before the wind. Brandon Enervold of {bse} doesn't like it any more than you would. But when a customer's pipe to the septic tank freezes, he gets the steamer set up, sits in the pickup and waits for it to warm up. Nobody wants to be out in it, he says, but when you have to be out in it, you have to.

#septic #septiclife #northdakota #winter #septicinstaller
captions.facebook:
I asked Brandon Enervold how cold it gets in Bismarck, North Dakota. His answer: 40 below, and then they add wind on that. You'd think the work would just stop, but it doesn't. The snow still has to be moved, and the cattle waters freeze. When somebody's septic pipe freezes on the way to the tank, Brandon gets his steamer set up, sits in his pickup and waits for it to warm up. Nobody wants to be out in it, he said, but when you have to be out in it, you have to.

#septic

I asked Brandon Enervold what he'd tell himself if he could go back to 2009, when he first got into septic. His answer: get more marketing going faster. He thinks it would have helped him scale a lot sooner, and he still doesn't think he's doing enough. He's worked hard on his reviews the last few years, but if he were starting a business today, advertising and reviews would be the number one thing he'd go after, more than the work. His reason stuck with me: your friends already know about you. You have to get the rest of the world to find you. Thank you, {bse}.
